questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was relevant for my studies.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Everything was send on email, more than once, so it was very easy to find the information as long as you made sure to read all the emails carefully, since a lot of information gets send out.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't really receive any assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It didn't take that long, but I also had to contact quite a few places and was in a hurry, since I was going travelling, so I didn't have time to look further. I would recommend going to Korea and search while in the country as it is easier and more helpful in finding a nice place.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There are always many goshiwons near the universities, so if you can't get on campus housing it will be easy find other housing off campus. Despite goshiwons being small, it is possible to find some really decent ones if you just keep looking.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: All the information gets send to you via email for both undergrad and graduate courses. So I just followed the guide and saved the names and course codes for the courses, which made it easy to sign up.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It was always possible to write the global service center and ask them for help if needed. They answered within a day.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I registered for all the classes I wanted. And for the other classes I considered taking, it was possible to ask the professor during the introduction week if it would be possible to participate.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just follow the emails and ask if you have any questions, then it will be really easy and simple.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Despite the courses feeling a little bit harder and more demanding than in Denmark, I wouldn't say the level of the courses was that much different. There was a lot more homework in terms of reading material than I'm used to and the amount of work that has to be submitted throughout the semester was also fairly larger than in DK.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Most of the courses expected the students to participate and take control of the class, so that the professor kind of worked like a meditator. There was a lot of presentations from the students and not that many lecture style classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: I took Emerging Media, Film Theories and History and Theories of Cultural Studies all at the Graduate School of Media and Communication.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't take any exchange student only courses, thus I was for the most part the only exchange student in my class, however all of the professors were really helpful and very kind, so I would recommend taking any courses that you're interested in. In particular for the courses I took, Film Theories was really good and the professor was very engaging and encouraging everyone.

Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They had clubs and also activities both cultural and social for exchange students through KUBA.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't do any, since everyone was mostly undergrad students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: If there is time, I would definitely recommend travelling outside of Seoul.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Since I've been there many times I had zero problems adjusting.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It is definitely easier if you take regular courses and not exchange students courses, if you want to talk with them.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Most Koreans are really friendly and helpful.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Read the emails carefully, since all information is send via email. Be open towards new people and new experiences.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nothing I can think of right now.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Gaining a lot of new knowledge as well as some very close friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finals.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
